title: Minimum number of repeated sizes needed in a cube dissection

problemStatement.plain: What is the minimum number of cubes that must participate in size collisions in any cube dissection? We prove ≥ 2 and ask whether exactly 2 is achievable (HasMinimalCollision).
whyMatters: Quantifies 'how far from perfect' a cube dissection must be
Connects impossibility theorem (Wiedijk #82) to an open minimization problem
2D analog (squared squares) allows all different sizes, so dimension matters

proven: every_dissection_has_collision: every nonempty dissection has a collision pair
collision_class_at_least_two: size class of a colliding cube has ≥ 2 members
at_least_two_colliding_cubes: collidingCubes.card ≥ 2 for any nonempty dissection
open: HasMinimalCollision: is there a valid dissection with exactly 2 colliding cubes?
smaller_cube_above_axiom: smallest cube on floor forces smaller cubes above (requires 3D geometric covering)
all_different_implies_long_chains_axiom: depends on smaller_cube_above (axiom in base file)
knownResults.goal: Determine minimum collidingCubes.card over all valid cube dissections

insights: A collision pair (c1, c2) contributes BOTH cubes to collidingCubes — each witnesses the other
Classical.decEq is required for Finset.filter on Cube (real-valued structure, equality not decidable)
covers_unit_cube : True is a placeholder that makes any Finset Cube a valid dissection — real geometry not captured
The geometric cascade (floor argument) suggests the true minimum is much larger than 2
2D allows all-different sizes (squared squares), so the 3D impossibility is dimension-specific
Finset.card_pair requires c1 ≠ c2 explicitly; Ne.symm handles the symmetric inequality in the proof
mathlibGaps: Real number equality is not decidable constructively — Classical.decEq required throughout
